headline: What Mistakes to Avoid When Rebuilding After Home Water Damage
articleBody:
Discovering soaked baseboards or water pooling under cabinets is stressful, and rushing to patch the cosmetic damage without proper steps creates bigger issues later. Protecting your home requires patience and a structured approach to drying and restoration.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Rebuilding before framing is completely dry: Nailing fresh drywall or laying vinyl plank over damp wood studs traps moisture inside wall cavities. The EPA emphasizes drying wet materials within 24 to 48 hours to stop mold growth; verify wood is dry with moisture meters before hanging boards.
- Stepping into flooded rooms without checking hazards: Standing water can hide live electrical currents or compromised subfloors. Always switch off power to the affected zone at the breaker panel before inspecting wet areas.
- Tossing soaked materials before taking photos: Tearing out ruined carpet or drywall before capturing photos can jeopardize your insurance claim. Document every damp surface thoroughly from multiple angles before starting cleanup.
- Painting over ceiling and wall water rings: A coat of standard interior paint will not hold back water damage. Trapped moisture softens gypsum cores, causing sagging and eventual collapse if damaged sheetrock is not cut out and replaced.
- Neglecting hidden moisture behind baseboards: Water wicks upward behind walls and under cabinets. Simply drying surface tile leaves dampness inside wall cavities where it steadily degrades structural studs.

What to Do Next
